assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only peach-girl:kashiwagi-sae@manga#second-pass-character-monograph (PEACH_GIRL_SAE_MONOGRAPH.md, version 1.2, active_provisional) and peach-girl:kashiwagi-sae@manga#time-indexed-literary-dossier (PEACH_GIRL_SAE_TIME_INDEXED_RECONSTRUCTION_DOSSIER.md, version 0.1, active_provisional) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the original Japanese 新装版 manga V01-V18. The Peach Girl current-state and corpus map was read for method, authority order and scope only. The volume readings, the four longitudinal ledgers, the second-pass audit, reconciliation, coverage and reconstruction reassessments, the G4 rules, cases, results and runner, and the other characters' monographs and dossiers are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. The project's BOUNDED_PROVISIONAL, PASS_SCOPED and BLOCKED_NO_HELD_OUT_VALIDATION labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime, live-action, sequel or related-manga material is included, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Thirteen dossier states from S01 (through V01 i0012) to S13 (V18 i0035-i0178), each bounded by an image cutoff, several spanning more than one volume (S06 V04-V05 i0044, S08 V06-V09 i0035, S09 V10-V12 i0168, S11 V15-V17 i0133), together with the monograph's V01-V18 developmental account. No default state is designated, so a cutoff must be named. Her life after the V18 ending, including future ethics, restitution, career and family, is expressly unestablished, and no in-world calendar dates are fixed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph states a governing reading (Sae Kashiwagi's most consistent capacity is to intervene in how other people interpret a scene, arranging who sees, hears or believes what) and tests it against located counterevidence: her interventions fail when Tōji checks the pool and Kairi Okayasu refuses the alliance (V01-V02), and later grief, protection and truthful disclosures resist a flat-villain reading. The dossier separates avowed from inferred goals per state. Both artifacts expressly leave motive mixed where the source does not discriminate rivalry, status, desire and enjoyment of disruption, and reject a fixed 'she only wants whoever Momo has' formula. Specialist interpretation; B is not supported because no conditional decision rules or motive ranking are given.

The dossier gives thirteen states S01-S13 with image cutoffs, a Known paragraph, conduct, and explicit exclusions (S02: definite receipt of Momo Adachi's real crush only at V01 i0073-i0080, with i0033 ambiguity unable to supply earlier knowledge; S11: she does not know Ryo Okayasu ordered the staged attack while offering a family; S12: mistaken pregnancy belief corrected by Ryo). The monograph orders the same development from copied tastes through V03 credibility collapse, V04 servility, V05 Tōji pursuit, V07 victimization, V13 targeted repair, V17 hammer attempt and shielding, to V18 truthful aid and forged farewell. A is not supported: the dossier is version 0.1, several states span multiple volumes, the thirteen vectors are unexecuted, and both artifacts come from the same second-pass authorship.

Register changes are tied to targets and occasions: familiar ももちゃん (also carrying a cosmetic approach or an intrusive question), the marked ももさま of the V04 i0116 servile episode, Ryo-sama at V13 i0034-i0035, polite uncle-address as V07 survival speech, the conditional threat 乱暴されたって先生に泣きついてやる (V03), halting ありがとう (V13), and 身体は正直ってこと at V18 i0140. The monograph states these support situational framing, not a universal deception detector, and that soft presentation does not prove a lie. There is more quoted wording than in comparable dossiers, but no register inventory, acoustic delivery or conversational model, so C is not supported; E is rejected because recipient-specific forms are located across the run.

Ordinary domains are located: the bag purchase and copied tastes (V01), modeling and editor responses, earnings, sales recruitment, cosmetics and perfume shopping (V05), school retakes and discipline, and parental blame and school-note requests (V18 i0012-i0014). The dossier's overlay says there is no complete career, legal, clinical or childhood-origin model and that sparse domains require abstention. These appear as context for schemes and crises rather than as routines, so C is not supported.

The dossier's overlay differentiates six domains, each with a stated limit: Momo (remembered recognition, rivalry, framing, rescue received, specific apology, continuing manipulation), Tōji (explicit desire, unwanted advances despite やめてくれ, impersonation, photo leverage), Kairi (antagonism, failed bargaining, aggression received, comfort and final device deception), Ryo (desired approval, money, hope of family, refused filming, betrayal knowledge, shielding), Misao (rival-blaming hostility, attempted violence, a promised boundary) and ordinary institutions and family. B is not supported: no matched-recipient decision rule is given and the family domain is sparse.

Interior claims rest mostly on Sae's avowals and actions: a private rank grievance (V01), a private complaint about the swimsuit scheme (V03), a V10 private disavowal with no securely named recipient, admitted envy and loneliness and a pictured family pledge (V17), and her V18 report of feeling lighter and no longer loving Ryo. Both artifacts present the pregnancy belief as apparently sincere rather than a scheme, and read her later defensive denial as contradicting her pledge. C is not supported because the evidence expressly leaves her motive undiscriminated and treats self-accounts as accounts at a time; E is rejected because located avowals and contradictions across volumes are analyzed.

Located conflict conduct is extensive and differentiated: relay alteration and staged witness (V01), the swimsuit sabotage by instruction and the conditional teacher-report threat (V03), incapacitation, impersonation and photographs (V05-V06), the palm slap of Momo while holding a vase after rescue (V07 i0031-i0045), renewed photo extortion, the hammer attempt on Misao stopped by Kairi (V17), and impersonated self-destructive urgency (V18). Actor guards are explicit (V08 fan, V09 hair singe, the old pool note). B is not supported: no escalation rule or conflict policy is stated.

The monograph distinguishes help from full reform, rescue from forgiveness, survival strategy from consent, and true information from permission for intrusive means (V14 arranged overhearing). Sae's own ethical reasoning is thinly evidenced: her criticism of the trio's dangerous punishment (V07), the scene-specific V13 apology and repair, and the V18 qualification that knowing about Kairi's search does not oblige a reunion. These are mostly the analyst's distinctions about her acts. C is not supported because no deliberation procedure is shown; E is rejected because recurrent located ethical structure exists.

The evidence mentions playful unusual modeling poses, chibi strain, cat forms and a final comic admission and chase without describing a humor or play repertoire. This gap says nothing about Sae's actual humor.

Both artifacts cover V01-V18 with image-coordinate routes (PG-JP-NE-VNN-W01/iNNNN) and route provenance to an all-18 source-first inspection of 3,198 images by four readers and an ordered reconciliation. The dossier states that its compiler directly read only V15-V18, with V01-V14 as attributed team evidence. The evaluator could not recheck the receipts, ledgers or readings, which are outside the set, and both artifacts disclose owner acceptance pending. B is not supported.

Affirmative limits and corrections are located: the V07 rescuer and slap recipient corrected from Kairi to Momo (PG-SA2-F0007), the old pool-note authorship kept unresolved, the V08 i0112 figure identified as an unnamed Kairi fan, V09 hair singe without proven order, the V03 threatened report not established as sexual or wholly false, the hospital near-kiss not completed, the pregnancy not established as knowingly fabricated, and Sae not the direct cause of Kairi's sea peril. Each is documented within these two same-authored artifacts and is not independently audited, so B is not supported.

Every state has an inclusive cutoff and separates character-known from reader-known information; the retrieval contract requires a named cutoff, recipient and situation and makes a missing cutoff an abstention condition. Vectors target leakage directly (S-VEC-01 at V01 i0034, S-VEC-06 V05 i0106 versus V06 i0099, S-VEC-10 V17 i0147 versus i0153, S-VEC-11 V18 i0120 versus i0176). A is not supported: no default state, coarser multi-volume spans, no in-world dates and unexecuted vectors.

scenario_readiness.note: The evidence analyzes a handful of situated written forms and states they are not interchangeable indicators of truth; it gives no conversational model or acoustic delivery. Lines written for Sae beyond the analyzed forms would be fluent invention rather than source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not Sae's actual speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Any named dossier state S01-S13 or V01-V18 cutoff; no post-V18 state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Any counterpart, including Momo, Tōji, Kairi, Ryo and Misao as the evidence describes them at the named cutoff; the refusal does not depend on the partner.
setting_constraints: Crossover, counterfactual or materially novel contexts outside the canon cutoffs
Adult career, legal, clinical or family-origin situations
Behavioral or dialogue simulation rather than retrieval of a canon state

scenario_readiness.note: The dossier says sparse domains require abstention, that it is neither the executable G4 policy nor an operationally accepted model, and that S-VEC-13 requires abstention on full redemption or deterministic relapse. Its states are retrieval cards for canon cutoffs, not a basis for a materially novel context.

Modeling, sales, school and family scenes are located only as context for schemes, crises and repair; no baseline for an unfamiliar ordinary scene is given. Bounded canon questions about the located episodes remain answerable.
The evidence analyzes completed acts and abstains on future ethics, restitution and reliable conduct after V18. No procedure for a new ethical choice by Sae can be run on this evidence set.

conditions: A dossier state S01-S13 or an equally exact V01-V18 cutoff is named; no default state is assumed and no information after the cutoff or unreceived by Sae is used.
The partner is Tōji (pursuit he refuses) or Ryo Okayasu (S09-S12) as the evidence describes him at that cutoff; Tōji's refusals remain refusals and her pursuit is never presented as reciprocity.
Output is a description of Sae's accessible knowledge, avowed and inferred goals and actual conduct, with the dossier's abstentions kept; no quoted dialogue is produced as canon.
Her V16-V17 pregnancy belief is treated as a mistaken belief, not a knowing fabrication, and her return to Ryo is not treated as retrospective consent.
No outcome after V18, renewed attachment to Ryo or future romance is asserted.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence differentiates her Tōji pursuit (V05 avowed desire through photo leverage) from the Ryo attachment (approval, money, hope of family, betrayal knowledge, shielding, grief and the V18 account of closure) by state. Readiness is conditional because the supported use is retrieval and bounded description at a canon cutoff, not prediction of a new romantic outcome; the vectors are unexecuted and operational acceptance is blocked.

Modeling, editor feedback, earnings and sales recruitment are located, but the dossier states there is no complete career model, and the V13 filming arrangement is analyzed as exploitation rather than ordinary work. No workplace behavior beyond the located episodes can be supported.

known_limits.statement: The dossier states it is neither the executable G4 policy nor an operationally accepted model; it organizes temporally bounded evidence for manual literary retrieval, and the monograph claims no operational reconstruction.

The thirteen S-VEC vectors are retrospective, unexecuted and not held out; they expose leakage and overgeneralization risks rather than reporting results, and operational acceptance is BLOCKED_NO_HELD_OUT_VALIDATION.

Known manipulation increases reasons to inspect provenance, not permission to assign Sae every anonymous act: the old pool note, the V08 i0112 smiling figure, the V09 hair singe and the V10 i0098 private recipient remain unattributed or unnamed.
Her motive is expressly left mixed where the source does not discriminate rivalry, status, desire and enjoyment of disruption; no single envy formula or motive ranking may be supplied.
Later disclosures (Ryo's ordered attack, the no-pregnancy explanation, her V18 authorship admission) cannot be installed in an earlier state; each state excludes later or unreceived information.

Her V18 account of feeling lighter and no longer loving Ryo is a current self-account, not permanent recovery; full redemption and deterministic relapse are both unsupported, and restitution is missing.

Both artifacts carry SECOND_PASS_SCOPED_SEMANTIC_REVIEW_PASSED_OWNER_ACCEPTANCE_PENDING, were authored and accepted within the project's own second pass, and are active_provisional; the dossier's compiler directly read only V15-V18.

The volume readings, four ledgers, source receipts, second-pass audit and reconciliation, coverage and reconstruction reassessments and the G4 rules, cases and results are not curated evidence on this subject, so their warrants and the project's preserved probe failures were not rechecked here. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
